A Premium Private Girls' School in Notting Hill, London
Pembridge Hall
A World-Class Girls' Education in Notting Hill
Pembridge Hall is a prestigious private school for girls in Notting Hill, London with a reputation for exceptional Preparatory and Pre-Preparatory education. We value each of our students as individuals and prepare them to thrive in a safe, happy and nurturing environment.
Widely recognised as one of London’s best girls’ schools, Pembridge Hall offers a well-rounded, inspiring curriculum that is supplemented by extensive extracurriculars, a strong pastoral-care programme, and specialist teachers who make learning an imaginative and inspiring experience. Our holistic approach means that pupils develop the self-esteem, resilience and love of learning that we believe is vital to success, and seamlessly transition to top day and boarding schools.
At our private girls' school in Notting Hill, ambitious academic standards and a strong sense of community inspire and motivate our students to develop their critical thinking, engage in creative and exploratory study, and master the skills needed to achieve their full potential.
Why Choose Our Private School in Notting Hill, London?
Pembridge Hall offers an excellent, well-rounded education for girls, with a curriculum designed to challenge and inspire. We believe that happy girls thrive, so we support our learners to explore their interests and passions with a wide range of extracurricular activities, alongside our innovative curriculum. At our girls’ school in London, we prepare learners for life by providing the necessary skills to excel in class and beyond, nurturing their confidence, resilience and self-esteem and instilling a lifelong love of learning.
Entry into Top Senior Schools
Our learners regularly go on to study at leading day and boarding schools
Over 60 Extracurricular Activities
Inspiring girls to explore their interests with a generous extracurricular offering
A Holistic Approach to Education
Cultivating excellence in class and beyond
A Nurturing Learning Environment
A child-centred ethos and strong pastoral care supports learners to reach their full potential

The academic results at Pembridge Hall are consistently impressive. We are a non-selective school, and use Cambridge Primary Insight (CPI) to conduct baseline standardised assessments and monitor progress, with internal assessments and formal exam preparation beginning from Year 3 onwards. Over the course of our students' time with us, we typically see a cohort average rise from the national average (an SAS of 100 in Reception) to a cohort average of around 125 in Year 6 - these figures far exceed the national average. Many girls achieve a score of 114 or above, or are considered exceptional, achieving a score of 127 or higher. We prepare our students to excel in their 11+ assessments, enabling them to go on to some of the top day and boarding schools in London, the UK and abroad.
Have a Developed Ability SAS of 111+ with 35% scoring in the top 4% nationally
Have a General Maths SAS of 111+ with 44% scoring in the top 4% nationally
Have a Reading SAS of 111+ with 24% scoring in the top 4% nationally
Pembridge Hall is part of Inspired, the leading education group that comprises top day and boarding schools in England, Europe, Africa and beyond. At our private school in Notting Hill, we equip girls to become curious, confident and multi-skilled learners, who embody the Pillars of an Inspired education – Academics, Sport, and Performing & Creative Arts. An ambitious curriculum, expert teachers and a generous extra-curricular programme support girls as they strive to unlock their full potential while leveraging the benefits of an international educational community.
Learn More About Inspired
Access to a Global Group of Premium Schools
Access to a Global Group of Premium Schools
Pembridge Hall, a top girls’ school in London, is one of over 110 premium schools across 26 countries in the Inspired portfolio. The world-leading education group has a record of delivering best practices in modern education. Inspired also aims to nurture well-rounded individuals who contribute to their local and global communities and achieve excellence in an ever-evolving world.
Dedicated Personalised Teaching
Dedicated Personalised Teaching
At our private school in Notting Hill, we hand-pick teachers who possess the required knowledge, commitment and dedication to inspire learners and guide them towards success. By adopting a personalised strategy, our educators support and challenge the children to achieve their individual academic goals and personal objectives, while also fostering a love of learning throughout their time with us.
Exclusive Summer Camps & Exchange Programme
Exclusive Summer Camps & Exchange Programme
With Inspired's summer camps and student exchange programmes, Pembridge Hall girls enjoy access to an international school community. These opportunities centre on sports, the arts, and academic and cultural pursuits, giving learners a broader perspective with which to understand the external environment.
Our girls' school in London follows a broad, innovative and highly respected curriculum, with memorable experiences led by subject specialists. Experienced educators guide learners to advance and hone their abilities in subjects like English, French, Music, Science, Art and Mathematics.

About Us
Nurturing Future Leaders with Exceptional Education
We provide girls with an ambitious, forward-thinking learning experience and cultivate their full potential with exceptional opportunities. At the end of their time with us, learners are curious, kind and well-rounded individuals who go on to attend some of the most prestigious day and boarding schools.
With a broad selection of enriching extracurriculars, girls are encouraged to pursue their unique interests, whether in sports such as netball, swimming, dance and fencing, or exciting club options, including Orchestra, Choir, Debating, Chess and Needlecraft.
We value our girls’ individuality and seek to empower them with positive personal qualities, including resilience, confidence and adaptability. As a school, we are dedicated to fostering enquiring and disciplined minds, transforming girls into successful learners and thinkers, and equipping them for their future roles in society.
Laying the Foundations for Success in Class and Beyond
A very warm welcome to Pembridge Hall, where we are proud to say that our girls are at the heart of all we do. We believe that self-esteem, resilience and happiness are paramount to every child's success, and we pride ourselves on developing confident individuals with a love of learning and a thirst for knowledge.
Our students benefit from extensive opportunities to learn both inside and outside the classroom. We proudly provide girls with a ‘three-dimensional education’, believing it is only when teaching is inspiring and imaginative that girls will truly thrive. Ambitious academic standards, a talented staffroom, and strong pastoral care all contribute to the success that our girls attain. Sport and the Arts feature strongly in the curriculum, enabling learners to become skilled across many facets. We are proud to be a London-based school and appreciate all the rich, exciting opportunities that surround us.
Teachers, students and parents work in a close partnership to ensure each girl is happy and achieving her maximum potential. At the end of Year 6, girls transfer to some of the finest senior day and boarding schools in the country, such as Godolphin and Latymer, St Paul’s Girls and Wycombe Abbey.
In a rapidly changing world, we offer an excellent, all-rounded education that prepares students for life, while also ensuring they experience a childhood they will cherish. If you are looking for a school that will bring the best out of your daughter, please do come and visit us during an Open Morning to see first-hand what makes us so special.
Mrs Sophie Banks, Head
Our Mission
Our pupils are at the heart of all we do. We emphasise each student's individuality, recognising that happiness, a love of learning and emotional well-being are intrinsic to strong academic performance. By combining traditional values with an innovative education, we provide girls with an ambitious, aspirational school experience, which not only nurtures and challenges them but also empowers them to succeed.
Our Values
We encourage learners to strive to achieve their personal best while also developing their unique character. Learners are seen as individuals. Their interests and talents are nurtured, while they themselves are pushed to be confident and articulate, and to understand the importance of humility.
Learners develop the skills to work collaboratively with one another, using emotional intelligence and a toolkit of strategies to support both themselves and others. They also learn empathy and a sense of self-understanding.
Learners are stimulated to be intellectually curious, ask questions, and develop a love of learning. We provide them with a breadth of experiences and encourage them to aim high in all they do.
We teach our learners to understand the importance of making mistakes and push them to step out of their comfort zone in their learning. Our progressive curriculum fosters a culture of striving for excellence, and families are supported to be aspirational in their senior school choices.
Girls have many opportunities to reflect on their learning and create strategies to manage their well-being. They enjoy challenges, take risks and develop a growth mindset.
Our students gain an appreciation of wider society and the diversity of nationalities, faiths, beliefs and languages represented by our families. They develop a sense of responsibility when it comes to helping others, including through charitable work and community outreach.
An Inspiring Curriculum
Our ambitious, tailored curriculum is designed to stimulate, challenge and inspire girls from an early age.
In pre-preparatory school, we teach learners to participate actively in the education process, which at this stage includes physical, social and academic opportunities and is enhanced by creative and exploratory learning areas.
Years 1 and 2 follow an accelerated version of the National Curriculum involving a mix of independent and teacher-guided work. At the preparatory level, children are thrilled to embark on a rich, balanced course of study, becoming independent, critical thinkers while also taking on greater responsibilities. Preparation for the 11+ and Common Entrance exams begins in Year 5.
Once the girls have completed these assessments in Year 6, they continue to engage deeply in a varied, all-rounded curriculum, which prepares them to make a seamless transition to top senior schools.
Student Testimonials

We learn about lots of different technologies in Computing. I especially love coding, gaming and exploring other worlds with VR goggles.
I love playing different pieces of music during my flute lessons and taking part in performances. Playing music makes me feel happy.

Careers
Join a fast-paced, dynamic school culture that inspires academic excellence for girls and is dedicated to fostering your professional growth. At Pembridge Hall, innovation and teamwork are at the heart of everything we do. Every girl aspires to achieve her best, creating an inspiring classroom environment. Our supportive culture fosters creativity and shared success. With a strong emphasis on Continuing Professional Development and career advancement, Pembridge Hall empowers educators to grow and excel in their careers.
Learn More about Pembridge Hall
Part of Inspired Education
At Inspired Education, we offer an exceptional opportunity to join the world’s leading premium school group and shape the future of education.
Purpose & Growth Journey Join a global community with an unwavering commitment tot empowers over 90,000 students across 26 countries. As the fastest-growing education group, your contributions will directly impact our journey of continuous global expansion and excellence.
Career Development We believe in nurturing talent and offering endless possibilities for career advancement. With Inspired, you will have access to opportunities across our 118 schools, enabling you to pursue your ambitions on a global scale. 31% of our educators take on exciting new roles overseas, and over 26% of our head appointments are made from within.
Global Community & Collaboration You will become part of a diverse, inclusive team of more than 12,000 professionals from over 109 nationalities. Together, we cultivate a culture of respect, dignity, and inclusion, where your talents and experiences are valued and celebrated.
Leaders in EdTech & Innovation We are transforming education through advanced technology and cutting-edge innovation. We invest more than any other school group in AI, EdTech, and immersive learning, enabling our educators to personalise learning paths and improve student outcomes.
State-of-the-Art Facilities Our campuses are designed to reflect our progressive approach to education. You will work in an environment that encourages exploration, creativity, and student engagement. With access to the latest tools and technologies, you will have the resources to inspire and motivate students, helping them to thrive in a rapidly evolving world.
A Culture of Innovation & Growth We foster a growth mindset that extends beyond our students to our entire community. Together, we are shaping a future where education is dynamic, inclusive, and always evolving.
Learn More about Inspired Careers

Pembridge Hall Parents’ Association
Enriching School Life with an Engaged Parent Body
The primary aim of the Pembridge Hall Parents’ Association (PHPA) is to enhance the girls’ overall experience at school by arranging various events throughout the academic year. In affairs relating to charitable giving, the group raises awareness of our chosen initiatives and takes steps to involve students in fundraising activities. Additionally, the PHPA oversees communication between the school and parents with regard to social matters.
Coordination between the girls and parents is facilitated via our dedicated Class Reps. Each class has a Class Rep, one of whom is the Year Rep, and their role is to organise and raise support for events in addition to communicating with the PHPA. Meetings of the PHPA Committee are held twice a term, and the minutes thereof are distributed to all parents.
Discover more about our engaged parent body and how they enrich and contribute to school life.

Pastoral Care
Fostering Critical Values in a Safe, Nurturing Environment
At Pembridge Hall, we are proud to promote positive personal qualities in our girls and foster their welfare and well-being as part of our robust pastoral care programme. We offer a nurturing environment for our learners to gain key life skills in, equipping them for success both in class and beyond.
Considerable emphasis is placed on the importance of good manners, excellent behaviour and personal responsibility, and we incorporate these values into all areas of school life. These core attributes are supported by our Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHEE) initiative and the creation of safe, caring learning conditions.
The interventions below are in force to support students with effective pastoral care, which in turn helps them to become independent and live confidently as active, informed and responsible citizens.
Building Ownership with Impactful Initiatives
Girls at Pembridge Hall are empowered to make meaningful contributions to school life, building confidence and a sense of ownership of their community. There are many opportunities for learners to participate in impactful activities, including our House system, Green Girls, School Council and Food Council.
Holistic Education that Prioritises Mental Health and Well-Being
Our girls benefit from a holistic approach to education, in which students' mental health and well-being are prioritised. By supporting these elements during early development, we provide learners with the necessary tools to strengthen both their self-esteem and capacity for self-regulation. Promoting these faculties also allows them to engage positively with their education and maximise excellence in academic performance.
A Safe Environment that Maximises Potential
Children have a right to feel safe, cared for and supported at school. Our experienced educators work hard to maintain suitable learning conditions and to protect all students as a matter of urgency. By creating an environment that prioritises safeguarding, we offer a foundation for our learners that facilitates their development and maximises their academic potential.
Combating Radicalisation with Fundamental British Principles
As part of our school's Safeguarding and Child Protection mandate, we shield learners from extremism and radicalisation by promoting British values and ensuring all staff adhere to and are trained in the Government’s Prevent Duty.
Resilience to such threats as those mentioned is ingrained in our ethos, curriculum and enrichment activities. As a British school, we expect learners to embody certain core principles, including democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and cultures. Additionally, teachers are equipped to identify pupils at risk of radicalisation and the relevant safeguarding pathways to be implemented.
A Secure Approach to Learning Technologies
Modern technology can significantly enrich school life, provided they are leveraged in a safe and secure manner. At Pembridge Hall, we have a robust eSafety policy to ensure the responsible use of all learning technologies (including the internet, mobile phones, collaboration tools and personal publishing) from Reception up to Year 6.
In Computing lessons and the broader curriculum, learners are taught about the risks and benefits of using technology, with specific concepts learnt at appropriate age levels. We also collaborate with Childnet International, a non-profit organisation dedicated to making the internet safe and enjoyable for children. These vital interventions provide students with awareness and safeguards and empower them to control their experiences online, an important skill both in class and beyond.
Formal mechanisms are in place to ensure that all eSafety issues are reported and recorded. In addition, our school supports parents with regular workshops on online safety strategies, advertised in advance.

Scholarships & Bursaries
Nsouli Scholars
A Transformative Opportunity
The Nsouli Scholars Programme is an exciting global initiative that promises to transform lives by enabling 50 extraordinary students at any one time to attend any of Inspired’s prestigious schools on a full scholarship for the duration of their education. The ambition is that the scholarship will provide hundreds of children with an opportunity to receive a truly transformative education.
By opening this path to exceptional individuals, we hope to expand our community, and to empower children of all backgrounds with unrivalled opportunities in academics, sports, the arts and extracurricular activities. In this sense, the Nsouli Scholars Programme is an investment both in education and in shaping the leaders of tomorrow.
This generous endowment honours Nadim Nsouli, who founded Inspired in 2013 as a definitive statement of excellence in private international education. In recognition of Mr Nsouli’s Lebanese heritage and Inspired’s commitment to inclusivity, several scholarships will be awarded to individuals of Lebanese origin.
Inspired schools offer a world-class educational experience that combines academics and engaging extra-curricular activities, producing confident, multi-skilled students who flourish in a competitive and increasingly interconnected world. Along with expert instruction by hand-picked teachers, our students access specialist sports programmes and professional tutelage from leaders in the performing and creative arts. As a result, they leave armed with a robust value system and a love of learning that extends well beyond the classroom.
Inspired is also committed to leveraging new and transformative learning technologies. Inspired AI empowers children to achieve academic excellence by delivering actionable insights that are unique to each student, including strengths and weaknesses. Our partnership with The Royal College of Music and Forte, a revolutionary online platform, enables children to receive personalised music tuition from professionals. Students with musical interests benefit from bespoke private lessons, advancing their practice as creatives and gaining valuable performance experience.
The advantages of our holistic approach to education are evidenced by the fact that Inspired students consistently excel in academic performance, surpassing national and global averages. In 2022, the Average Point Score was 35 for those undertaking the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, for which the world average was 31.98, while A* scores comprised 27% of our students' A Level grades, compared to 14.6% globally. As a consequence, many are able to attend leading universities, with one in three graduates going on to a Russell Group University or Ivy League College.
The Inspired Group includes top-rated day and boarding schools worldwide, meaning students enjoy access to a diverse international community. Be it through specialised Summer Camps or immersive Global Exchange Programmes, children have the chance to travel broadly and engage meaningfully with different cultures, meet and learn from our esteemed partners, build lifelong networks, and become more independent.
Financial Support
By welcoming students from different backgrounds, we create spaces that are inclusive, engaging and rich in all manner of potential learning opportunities. As such, we are eager to support extraordinary learners who, from a means perspective, are unable to access an exceptional education. We warmly invite families to apply for financial support for their child to join our magnificent private school in Notting Hill.
Growing our School Community with Funding for Deserving Applicants
We are immensely proud of the opportunities that we offer and the many extraordinary girls whose successes, interests and individuality we help cultivate. It is our wish that other learners, outside our current community, can achieve excellence by receiving a bursary to our exceptional school.
Bursaries for Pembridge Hall students are administered by the Gold Standard Charitable Trust (GSCT), which raises money for all Inspired UK Schools. The Head will put short-listed candidates in touch with GSCT, which conducts a means test as part of the application process. Awards for successful applicants range between 50% and 110% of the cost of tuition.
Take the First Step Towards Unlocking your Child's Full Potential
To begin your child's journey to an exceptional future, apply for a bursary to our school via the button below.
Learn more about our bursary programme and how it can unlock your daughter's full potential.

Enquire Now
Start Your Daughter's Inspiring Academic Journey Today

An Inspired School
Inspiring Excellence to Expand Horizons
At Pembridge Hall, we are proud to be part of Inspired Education, a leading global group of 121 premium schools educating 95,000+ students on 6 continents. Inspired provides learners with a dynamic, holistic learning experience, fostering excellence and opening doors with exciting and wide-ranging opportunities. As a school, we share this commitment to success in many areas, offering cutting-edge teaching practices, unrivalled extracurriculars and co-curricular activities, and access to a rich global school community. Thus, girls are empowered to excel both in class and as confident, independent, multi-skilled individuals.
The Pillars of an Inspired Education
An Inspired education is based on a holistic philosophy that extends well beyond traditional academia. This approach is focused on three key Pillars, which equip learners with exceptional abilities: Academics, Sport, and Performing & Creative Arts. By integrating each Pillar into the learning process, Inspired helps students to develop impeccable leadership qualities, sound study methods and the ability to manage their time across many disciplines. Learners emerge armed with a broad skill set, which enables them to achieve excellence both in class and in the wider world.
Academics is the central Pillar of an Inspired education. Inspired’s commitment to academic excellence allows learners to develop a range of proficiencies, such as comprehension, lateral thinking, and the innovative application of skills and concepts. In addition to excelling in formal assessments, students gain up-to-date knowledge, become lifelong learners, and are fully equipped to succeed both in class and the wider world.
Performing and Creative Arts
Performing and Creative Arts
The Performing and Creative Arts Pillar is key to a holistic, integrated education. Inspired schools teach learners to appreciate the arts and participate actively in creative self-expression, be it dance, drama, music or visual art. As a result, learners become confident and are empowered to explore their unique interests and passions, while also developing as individuals.
Sport allows students to gain positive personal qualities, like teamwork and discipline, while also developing their overall well-being. As an Inspired school, we offer various sports to promote mental and physical health in a fun, stimulating setting, from swimming and dance to fencing and netball.

Girls' Pre-Prep School in Notting Hill, London
An Ambitious Education at Our Notting Hill Pre-Prep School
Welcome to our Pre-Prep school in Notting Hill, West London, where girls aged 4 to 7 are inspired to reach their full potential and we are passionate about every pupil getting the best possible start to their education. We view each child as an individual, and our holistic early learning programme prioritises their wellbeing, alongside their academic development.
Our girls benefit from wonderful specialist facilities as well as exceptional teaching staff, and the bright and airy classrooms of 18 Pembridge Square are an ideal place to learn.
In Reception, we aim to challenge our girls academically with structured literacy and maths sessions, as well as promoting learning through creativity and exploration. Learners in Years 1 and 2 follow an accelerated version of the National Curriculum, which encourages them to be aspirational in their studies. Above all, we want the children in our care to feel happy and safe, and develop a lifelong passion for learning.
Life at Pembridge Hall is full of opportunity, ensuring that girls emerge from our private Notting Hill Pre-Prep school as independent, confident and well-rounded individuals.
Why Choose our Pre-Prep School, London?
Children at our Pre-Prep school in Notting Hill enjoy a wide range of educational opportunities right from the start of their time with us.
This is a crucial part of your child's school career, and why at Pembridge Hall we take a personalised approach to each girls' unique learning journey. The high standards we cultivate and maintain throughout the school mean that many of our students either exceed or perform exceptionally in their Standard Age Score (SAS) assessments, laying the foundations for future academic success.
Our principal aim is to instil a lifelong passion for learning in all our students and we want them to feel safe and happy. We know that young children learn best when they are motivated through playful experiences and are given the chance to direct their own learning. Our robust early education programme provides for this, while also supporting individual learning styles and needs.
Pre-Preparatory School Curriculum
At our prestigious Pre-Prep in Notting Hill, our ambitious curriculum helps students to succeed both in their studies and life outside school, as confident and well-rounded individuals. A dynamic, academically rigorous environment promotes high achievement, and learners gain confidence, independence and ambition so that they may achieve their full potential.
Reception
In Reception, we aim to challenge our students academically, and we do this by incorporating creative and exploratory learning areas, alongside structured programmes that promote literacy and mathematics.
Years 1 and 2
An accelerated version of the National Curriculum is taught at our pre-prep school, including French from Year 1 and music lessons from Year 2. In addition to challenging learners through structured physical, social and academic opportunities, this bespoke syllabus encourages students to actively participate in their education and cultivates their natural curiosity through fun and engaging experiences. From Year 2, they also have the added excitement of weekly Science lab and Swimming sessions, which are both taught by our specialist teachers.
Language Immersion in Pre-Prep School
Language education at our school serves to develop learners' communication skills, along with their appreciation of other world cultures. In Reception, language is taught through a structured curriculum that includes key elements like Reading, Writing and Phonics. Lower School takes this further with girls benefitting from French and English lessons. Outside the curriculum, girls are invited to join clubs with a language focus from Year 1 onwards, such as French and Mandarin, to advance their knowledge and comprehension. By immersing themselves at this Pre-Prep level, girls are then able to continue their language studies in Middle and Upper School.
Pre-Prep School Facilities
Our beautifully repurposed Georgian buildings in the heart of Notting Hill feature bright, airy classrooms, and a comfortable, nurturing space in which to learn and grow.
We have a range of specialist teaching facilities, including an Art Studio, Music Room, and a custom-built, interactive Science Laboratory.
We have dedicated areas for exercise and play during morning break times, including three separate areas in Number 18, and gated gardens in the centre of Pembridge Square.
Early Education Teachers
Our skilled Reception and Lower School teachers are an essential part of our high-quality pre-prep provision. We carefully select staff who are experts in Early Education, display skill and a strong educational ethos, and are passionate about teaching and learning. As a result, our girls are supported and challenged in a unique and exciting environment for aspirational learning, and each teacher is dedicated to developing our young scholars, helping to ensure they reach their full potential.
Extracurricular Activities at our Pre-Prep School
Our Pre-Prep in Notting Hill presents girls with a diversity of extracurricular options, which offer invaluable opportunities for both growth and accomplishment. Developing our girls as individuals is extremely important to us; by delivering an all-rounded experience, we empower them to become confident, driven and multi-skilled, and broaden their horizons both in school and in life beyond.
From Year 1 onwards, learners are invited to develop their personal interests and proficiencies by participating in various sport and club activities, which take place in the afternoon. Among the sports offered are football, dance, yoga and gymnastics. Opportunities like these are essential for fostering girls’ physical and mental well-being, and promote life skills like teamwork and discipline. Girls with a flair for performance or creativity can enrol in exciting club options, including Art, Jewellery Making and Junior Choir, building confidence, gaining new insights and artistic abilities, and advancing their prospects in their field of choice. Scientific reasoning and technical skills are also fostered in clubs like Mathletics and Computer Crazy.
For further details on our generous sport and club offering, please visit Extracurricular Activities.
Co-Curricular Activities
Our Notting Hill Pre-Prep school is committed to providing an ambitious early education programme. From Reception at Pembridge Hall, learners are privileged to explore co-curricular activities that supplement their main course of study. Students take part in organised school trips, which are linked to (and enhance learning in) topics in the core curriculum. Additional highlights include themed events, like Scottish Day, half-termly outdoor learning, musical concerts, a fun-filled Sports Day and our delightful Easter hat parade.
Learn more about our magnificent Pre-Prep and how a progressive, aspirational education can unlock your child's full potential.

Girls' Prep School in Notting Hill, London
Outstanding Prep Education in Notting Hill
Girls joining our Notting Hill Prep school are met with a wide variety of inspirational learning experiences. Our progressive Prep curriculum supports girls aged 7 to 11 and challenges them to unlock their full potential as academically accomplished, well-rounded individuals.
A dynamic and carefully planned educational programme guides pupils to outstanding achievements through leading academic provision and exam preparation. Many of our girls secure places at some of the top day and boarding schools in London, across the UK and beyond.
At our girls' Prep school in Notting Hill, we offer extensive extracurricular and co-curricular activities. In addition to challenging, inspiring and stimulating learners, these opportunities foster a diverse, in-demand skill set while cultivating learners’ unique talents.
Robust pastoral care at our Notting Hill Prep school instils valuable qualities, including independence, resilience, self-esteem, respect and humility, preparing learners for life outside Pembridge Hall.
Why Choose our Prep School in Notting Hill?
An education at our premium girls' school in Notting Hill seeks to inspire, nurture and challenge pupils, providing a wealth of opportunities and empowering students to excel both in the classroom and outside of school. We develop our girls as individuals, with outstanding academic and pastoral support that encourages confidence, curiosity, ambition and takes a well-rounded approach to learning.
As well as a rigorous and inspiring curriculum, extracurriculars feature prominently in our Prep-school offering, ensuring that students of all skills and abilities can flourish in our nurturing and welcoming school environment.
We teach our students the importance of diligence and organisation, ensuring that they understand the need to prepare for the future, think independently and take an appropriate level of responsibility for their learning. Older pupils are expected to serve as role models for their younger counterparts and all students contribute to the wider school community.
At our girls' Prep school in Notting Hill we prepare students to transition to top day and boarding schools across the UK and beyond.
Our Prep School Curriculum
At our girls' Prep school in Notting Hill, we offer an innovative and ambitious curriculum, delivered by brilliant educators who empower our girls to do their best, fostering a relaxed and open atmosphere.
In Years 3-4, pupils develop a strong sense of academic responsibility, while in Years 5-6, we support each student as they rigorously prepare for their 11+ examinations. At this stage, we place greater emphasis on enquiry and critical thinking, while practical lessons cultivate their creativity and help them gain broader life skills and appreciate the interconnectivity between subjects. This varied programme allows pupils to move seamlessly into senior school.
Prep School Facilities
Our exquisite repurposed Georgian building at 10 Pembridge Square feature a range of excellent facilities.
Fully equipped and custom-built for a premium Preparatory education, our specialist spaces allow for engagement in various educational opportunities. We have a purpose-built Science Laboratory and an Innovation Space, housing robotics equipment, a green screen and virtual reality goggles to support creativity and project-based learning. Learners can also participate in physical activities using our spacious Gymnasium. Our light and airy Art Studio and Drama Studio (complete with stage lighting and a dazzling array of costumes and props) give children the opportunity to explore and develop in the performing and creative arts.
Language Immersion at Preparatory Level
Language is a key element of our Prep-school offering, allowing students to become skilled communicators and promoting appreciation of other cultures. We offer a range of languages in our core curriculum. As well as taking English as a subject, learners continue to develop their fluency in French, and can also explore Spanish and Latin. In addition, they can expand their knowledge by enrolling in any of our clubs devoted to languages.
Prep School Teachers
At our Preparatory school in Notting Hill, we believe that our skilled staff are the key to our success. Our hand-picked Middle and Upper School teachers are highly motivated and will ensure that your child is challenged and prepared for future education. Our teachers have excellent qualifications in their field, dynamic personalities and a professional bearing. As a result, our girls enjoy learning and flourish in the nurturing, Pembridge Hall environment.
Extracurricular Activities for Preparatory Students
At our girls’ Preparatory in Notting Hill, children are encouraged to explore and develop their unique skills. We provide girls with a host of exciting extracurriculars, from sports and the arts to language and cultural activities, all of which are designed to inspire and nurture them as individuals.
Netball is our primary sport as a school and we are incredibly proud of our exceptional players, who recently went on tour to Dubai. As our school enjoys access to Paddington Recreation Ground and Kensington Leisure Centre, learners also participate in football, hockey, cricket and rounders.
Among the many clubs that we offer our girls, the creative and performing art options such as Art Portfolio, Movie Making, Needlecraft and Musical Theatre, allow students to really elevate their skills with training from specialist educators.
We also invite girls with proven abilities to enrol in invitation-only groups. Swimming Squad, Orchestra, Advanced Netball and Chamber Choir are available solely at the Prep-school level and ensure children with extraordinary talents are supported and accommodated.
For the full list of clubs and sports that we offer as part of an ambitious, all-rounded education, please visit Extracurricular Activities
Co-Curricular Activities at our Prep School
Learning at our excellent Prep school in Notting Hill is enhanced by a broad co-curricular programme. Exciting workshops, trips and speakers offer an added layer of depth to the core curriculum, boost engagement, and inspire our girls to identify and pursue their unique interests.
In Middle School, children embark on their first-ever residential trip, arranged by a specialist team, in the company of peers and teachers. A major cross-curricular project – Thinking, Enterprise and Design Week – aims to develop the skills necessary to become entrepreneurs of the future. Weekly assemblies with competitions and musical performances solidify bonds between the different year groups.
Despite being academically rigorous, the Upper School years are highly rewarding and feature a full line-up of enjoyable day trips, outings and concerts for enrichment. Among the highlights of Year 6 are a week-long culturally immersive trip to France, a business and enterprise project, and a high-quality drama production.
Discover how a forward-thinking Prep school education could unlock your child's full potential and help them achieve success at school and beyond.

Extracurricular Activities
Unleashing your Child's Full Potential with a Diversity of Enriching Opportunities
Our holistic approach to education means that our young students enjoy a rich extracurricular programme, which is regarded as integral to school life. By pursuing their interests outside of traditional academia, our learners gain valuable personal qualities and abilities that benefit them both in class and beyond, such as confidence, teamwork, leadership, resilience, ambition and emotional intelligence. Moreover, through our comprehensive sport and club programmes, girls are challenged to hone their existing proficiencies and develop new ones. Diversifying and improving abilities is crucial when it comes to accessing top senior schools, where students' talents are further cultivated, and producing passionate, independent, curious and well-rounded individuals.
School Sports & Activities
All girls can participate in a range of sports and physical activities. With access to Paddington Recreation Ground and Kensington Leisure Centre, we are fully equipped to coach cricket, netball and rounders, among other sports. Selected girls join our elite Swimming Squad and Advanced Netball sessions, which take place in the early morning, and represent us in matches and galas throughout the school year. Younger students build their skills and fitness by playing fun ball-based games, meaning children of all ages are empowered in their mental, physical and social well-being.
Ballet
Our classes follow the Cecchetti standard syllabus, and girls are prepared to complete the corresponding examinations at the end of the Summer Term. Examinations are not mandatory, however, and children may choose to progress without taking them.
Dance
If you love dancing, this is the club for you. Participants explore a range of dance styles through music, games and activities. They also create their own group dances and solos, building their knowledge of body movement and improvisation as they go.
Fencing
Fencing is an exciting team and individual activity. It is a fast, dynamic non-contact Olympic sport with a martial-arts style and combines fitness and athleticism with technical skill and precision timing. Participants learn how to move in a balanced way with proper footwork, score hits with direct and indirect attacks, and defend using parries.
Gymnastics
Gymnastics is taught by a specialist company, and participants work on improving their flexibility, agility, coordination and spatial awareness. Upon joining the club, girls start with the basics, before going on to learn new skills, such as rolling, vaulting and balancing, throughout the term.
Netball
Years 3-6 (Netball) Years 5-6 (Advanced Netball - invitation only)
This club is aimed at all girls who are interested in playing Netball. They will develop their ball skills, footwork and tactics through a series of drills and match play. From here girls are selected according to ability to represent us against other schools.
Running
Running Club is an opportunity for the strongest runners in Years 5 and 6 to improve their stamina and technique for middle and long distances.
Swim Squad
Years 3-6 (invitation only)
All girls may trial for the Swim Squad at various points throughout the year. Those selected train with physical education (PE) staff and an external coach at the Porchester Centre in early morning sessions. They also represent us in galas and other competitions.
Yoga
Yoga teaches many valuable tools. In these classes, we go through some of the traditional poses and sun salutations to improve strength, flexibility and confidence. Participants are taught breathing exercises to aid with concentration and stress management, and partner and group yoga encourage respect and awareness of others. At the end of each class, we spend 5 minutes in ‘Savasana’ (mindfulness/meditation) using visualisation, which helps girls to relax, concentrate and practise self-awareness.
Clubs & Wraparound Care
Our girls benefit from an expansive club programme, which seeks to encourage and inspire them as individuals. With a sizeable weekly offering of over 70 clubs, we encourage our girls to pursue personal interests and discover new and enjoyable activities, thus developing in a variety of areas.
To support busy, working parents, we offer wraparound care for girls in Reception to Year 2, in conjunction with our club programme. Learners can attend Early Club from 8:00am and/or after-school sessions until 4:30pm (Reception to Year 2), 4:45pm (Years 3-4) and 5:00pm (Years 5-6), enjoying a range of activities and games, and meeting girls from other year groups.
Advanced Coding
In this club, girls will be doing advanced text-based coding using JavaScript. Students will be given the opportunity to build upon prior knowledge and be able to challenge themselves to get to grips with programming. They will also further their understanding of fundamentals, such as conditional logic, functions, loops and operators, developing fun and creative projects each week.
Art Club & Art Portfolio
Years 1-5 (Art Club) Year 6 (Art Portfolio - invitation only)
Every week, girls have the opportunity to express their creativity and use their imagination to produce different artworks.
Art Club allows them to extend their artistic proficiency by experimenting with various media and techniques, as well as being introduced to new artists. We use an array of tools and give students the freedom to interpret what they would like to make, paint or draw.
Art Portfolio is a selective club for girls who have shown ability in drawing and painting. They are encouraged to develop their skills further by attempting more advanced techniques through a series of exercises and projects.
Chess
Chess Club is suitable for all skill levels, and is a great way to have fun while learning to think for yourself and develop a healthy competitive spirit.
Coding
In this club, we introduce girls to text-based coding using JavaScript. Students learn to program by creating fun apps that work on computers and gadgets, like phones and tablets. They are also familiarised with fundamental concepts, such as conditional logic, functions, loops and operators, building visually exciting projects to engage them throughout the term and keep them excited to undertake new tasks each week.
Computer Crazy!
This club is a place for the girls to develop their computer literacy skills in an exciting and engaging format. Students explore and experiment with a variety of educational games. From practising coding to creating digital art and brushing up on their touch typing, there is something for everyone.
Cookery
Cookery Club by Smart Raspberry is a fantastic opportunity for children to develop the skills involved in cooking, as well as to experiment with different ingredients and, most importantly, enjoy food. Girls will make a wide variety of savoury and sweet dishes, some of which are ready to eat and some of which simply need to be cooked or heated at home. These classes will help participants to become more confident in the kitchen; increase their awareness of ingredients and encourage them to try foods they may not normally; practise maths and science in a creative way; learn more about hygiene; and have fun with food.
Debating
Would you like to be able to convince others of your ideas? In this club, you can learn the skill – and power – of debating: the art of putting forward a point of view with such persuasive force that listeners are minded to agree. By participating in a range of fun activities and games, students can improve their proficiencies as well as take part in formal, structured debates. There is no better way to increase your speaking and listening skills.
Drama
Come along to Drama Club to explore a plethora of stories, scripts and ideas. Participants get to experience directing, and develop their improvisation and collaboration skills. We also play exciting team games, and girls have the opportunity to devise their own performances and improvisations using props and costumes.
French
Club Petit Pierrot is our new external club provider. It allows the girls to learn in a lively, structured environment, through play and educational activities, and thus to explore, engage, experiment with, and master French without any undue pressure.
Homework
This club provides a space for girls to go and finish their homework under the supervision of a Middle/Upper School teacher. At Pembridge Hall, homework is used as a tool for the consolidation and reinforcement of concepts already learned. Therefore, while the supervising teacher will be able to support and answer clarifying questions, they will not be there in a 'teaching' capacity, as it is not a lesson. In Years 3-6, the expectation is that students can complete their schoolwork on their own. Once their work is completed, learners are expected to read independently until the end of the session.
Humanities
This is a great opportunity for girls to extend their learning by delving into the practical side of Humanities, including subjects such as R.E., History and Geography. Students are able to focus on a particular topic and use a variety of art and IT resources to advance their knowledge.
Jewellery Making
Girls attending this club will tap into their creative side, using an exciting variety of beads to make bracelets, necklaces, rings, headbands and hair clips that are designs of their own choice.
Junior Choir
Our junior girls explore a variety of songs and focus on the technical aspects of singing in a group, such as vocal projection and part singing.
Kitchen Sink Science
Participants in this club learn that, behind the magic of experiments with everyday kitchen ingredients, lies scientific proof. Girls will discover different aspects of biology, chemistry and physics through marvellous chemical reactions and engineering projects. From lava lamps to static electricity, this club offers many ways for learners to apply their knowledge to wider contexts, and they will soon realise that science is everywhere!
Lego
Lego Club allows the girls to explore their imagination and create their own sculptures in a relaxed yet purposeful environment. While working by themselves or with others to foster good communication and collaborative skills, they can choose to build something from a Challenge Card, develop their creativity and confidence, or work on their creations over a number of weeks.
Little House of Science
Our club provider Little House of Science will cover a different topic each week and provide demonstrations, activities and a take-home. Their curricula balance chemistry, biology, physics and engineering throughout each term.
This well-being club aims to provide girls with the opportunity to reflect, relax and build resilience. Each week, we will complete a variety of mindful activities, so that students learn more about embracing and managing different emotions. It will also allow them to explore friendships and the challenges that may come with making new friends and keeping them.
Mandarin
Mandarin Club is an exciting and informative way of introducing the Chinese language and culture to all girls from KS1 to KS2. A basic introduction offers a foundation to help them recognise and write Chinese characters, and memorise frequently used phrases. We foster enthusiasm for learning the language, while revealing the beauty of the associated culture through music and several traditional forms, such as calligraphy writing and paper art.
Mathletics
Our girls can enjoy the opportunity to extend and challenge themselves with the help of Mathletics. This involves working on age-appropriate Maths questions and games to gain points that will earn them a coveted Gold, Silver or Bronze Certificate.
Movie Making
In this club, learners direct, act in, or operate the camera in their very own film productions. We emphasise teamwork, embarking on various creative tasks and providing an exciting platform to explore different roles in filmmaking. From books and movie adaptations to live-action remakes, TV presenting, stop motion and more, this club is for those who love to perform and those interested in the technical side.
Musical Theatre
If you are a fan of musicals, this club is the one for you. In this musical theatre-themed class, we will be dancing to some of your favourite songs from Matilda, The Lion King, Wicked and more. Engaging in this form helps to highlight performance skills, such as connecting with the audience and facial expressions.
Needlecraft
These sessions allow girls to create their own designs, learn and refine sewing skills, and use stuffing and decorating accessories. Learners in Years 2 and 3 can choose to make pencil cases, bags or cushions, while Year 4-6 students design and produce aprons, skirts, tops or dresses.
Orchestra
Years 4-6 (invitation only)
This invitation-only club allows girls to enjoy shared music making with their peers. Our broad repertoire ranges from traditional melodies to modern classics by ABBA and helps prepare learners for forthcoming performances, such as our Carol Service and Summer Concerts.
Senior Choir
Every Wednesday before school, girls in Years 4-6 warm up their vocal chords, explore various songs and focus on part singing and vocal projection. Year 5 and 6 learners with proven ability may be accepted into our Chamber Choir.
Spanish Beginners
Hola! This club is aimed at girls who do not already speak Spanish. We cover the basics of the language using games and songs, and students can expect to learn greetings, numbers, colours, animals and more.
The Story Society
In this club, students will independently plan and write their own stories, producing a book that they can then keep. As the authors, they decide whether to write fiction or nonfiction, as well as selecting an appropriate genre. Over the term, they will illustrate their book, including creating an attention-grabbing front cover.

Pembridge Hall
A World-Class Girls' Education in Notting Hill
Pembridge Hall is a prestigious private school for girls in Notting Hill, London with a reputation for exceptional Preparatory and Pre-Preparatory education. We value each of our students as individuals and prepare them to thrive in a safe, happy and nurturing environment.
Widely recognised as one of London’s best girls’ schools, Pembridge Hall offers a well-rounded, inspiring curriculum that is supplemented by extensive extracurriculars, a strong pastoral-care programme, and specialist teachers who make learning an imaginative and inspiring experience. Our holistic approach means that pupils develop the self-esteem, resilience and love of learning that we believe is vital to success, and seamlessly transition to top day and boarding schools.
At our private girls' school in Notting Hill, ambitious academic standards and a strong sense of community inspire and motivate our students to develop their critical thinking, engage in creative and exploratory study, and master the skills needed to achieve their full potential.
Why Choose Our Private School in Notting Hill, London?
Pembridge Hall offers an excellent, well-rounded education for girls, with a curriculum designed to challenge and inspire. We believe that happy girls thrive, so we support our learners to explore their interests and passions with a wide range of extracurricular activities, alongside our innovative curriculum. At our girls’ school in London, we prepare learners for life by providing the necessary skills to excel in class and beyond, nurturing their confidence, resilience and self-esteem and instilling a lifelong love of learning.

Admissions Process
Begin Your Child's Journey to Unlimited Opportunities
Pembridge Hall is a prestigious non-selective school providing world-class education to girls aged 4 to 11. Set in a beautiful residential square, our school is a welcoming community that nurtures each student academically, creatively and pastorally.
With a reputation for excellence, places at our school are in high demand, and we are almost always full. As such, we advise prospective parents to apply well in advance of their desired year of entry.
Follow the simple steps below to apply for a place, and set your daughter on the path to success.
Submit Your Registration Form Today
Please complete the form below to register your interest in our school. Once you have registered, a member of the Admissions Team will contact you to provide further details of the application process.
Visit Our School
Parents of prospective students are invited to a school Open Morning two years before entry. The visit will take place during the day to provide a snapshot of school life. It is the ideal opportunity for parents to learn more about the benefits of a Pembridge Hall education and experience the environment first-hand.
Occasional places may become available for girls entering at points other than September of their Reception year. Please contact the Head of Admissions on 020 7229 0121 for further details on the admissions process.
Girls placed on the waiting list will be carried forward to the next academic year, at parents request.
Receiving an Offer
In June, one year prior to your child’s entry, an offer letter will be sent to the parents or legal guardians of successful candidates. To secure a place, a deposit equivalent to half a term's fees is required. The first term's fees will be invoiced in the term prior to enrolment.
Acceptance of Place
On acceptance of your child's place at Pembridge Hall, the Head of Admissions will be in contact to provide further welcome information.
For further information about our admissions process, please fill out an Enquiry Form. Our friendly team will be happy to help, and will get back to you as soon as possible.

FAQs
Learn More about Our Exceptional School
What are your school's entry points?
The main entry point to Pembridge Hall is Reception, where girls are admitted at 4 years old. However, we strongly advise prospective parents to register their child as soon after birth as possible. To ensure that birthdays are evenly distributed throughout the school year, we process applications by calendar month, dividing each month into thirds and selecting an even number of girls from each third at random. Places are allocated at the end of the month, after which names are added to our waiting list.
Girls hoping to enrol at age 7+ can attend our Assessment Day in the Spring Term. By assessing their Maths and English proficiencies, we can establish whether they are likely to adequately access and benefit from our curriculum's pace and breadth, which our Year 2 girls are accustomed to, having made significant academic progress in their three years at Pembridge Hall. Assessment Days also allow girls to familiarise themselves with our school and take part in a range of workshops with our specialist subject teachers.
Applications for girls in other years are subject to availability and require the completion of an age-appropriate assessment by prospective pupils, as well as reports from their feeder schools. Any reports or information from educational psychologists or other relevant bodies should also be supplied to assist the school with its decision.
Can I visit the school?
We warmly invite parents to learn more about our school by attending an in-person presentation by our Head, Mrs Sophie Banks, and Deputy Head, Miss Nicola Mooney. During this exclusive event, you can also meet and interact with the other members of our Senior Leadership Team, who will answer your questions and provide further information. You will then get a tour of the school to experience our facilities first-hand, followed by a meeting with our Year 6 students, who are happy to share experiences of their time at Pembridge Hall.
Can I meet the Head?
Once your child has been allocated a place at Pembridge Hall, you will be invited to visit the school and meet the Head, Mrs Sophie Banks, in person. Mrs Banks and the Deputy Head, Miss Nicola Mooney, can arrange a virtual meeting too, if this is preferable. You are also welcome to attend one of Mrs Banks's live virtual Q&A sessions for prospective parents, which are held throughout the school year.
What facilities does the school have?
Our beautiful Georgian buildings in Pembridge Square house an array of specialist rooms for conducting each curriculum subject lesson, along with facilities for extracurriculars. Both properties have form rooms and large, well-lit classrooms that serve as the ideal backdrop for learning and tuition. Students with an interest in the performing arts can develop their abilities in specifically designed creative spaces, such as the Music Room and Drama Studio. Our well-equipped Science Laboratory and Computing Suites allow girls to attain valuable technical skills, empowering them for success in a rapidly developing and interconnected world.
Despite having form rooms in different premises (Reception to Year 2 are based in 18 Pembridge Square and Years 3 to 6 in 10 Pembridge Square), students feel part of a single school community from a young age. Girls frequently move between buildings for specialist lessons, as well as making use of the stunning Princes Square Garden and Pembridge Gardens during playtimes.
To find out more about our magnificent facilities, please visit Our Campus page.
What are the advantages of a girls-only education?
Single-sex schools such as ours allow students to learn in, and benefit from, a supportive environment that accounts for sex-related differences in development, including rates of maturity and ways of learning at specific stages. As a result, we allow learners to delve deeper into the curriculum at an early age than at co-ed schools. Moreover, the majority of Senior Schools in west and central London are single-sex, making girls' prep schools the practical choice for some parents.
At Pembridge Hall, we firmly believe that there is no limit to what our girls are capable of. We encourage them to speak up and ask questions, while also challenging all gender stereotypes.
Which senior schools do Pembridge girls move on to?
Over seven years at Pembridge Hall, girls are empowered to excel academically in their 11+ entry papers, allowing for a seamless transition into the next stage of their schooling. Our exceptional teachers and learning opportunities prepare girls to successfully advance to some of the leading day and boarding schools in London, the UK and beyond. We have well-established links with destination senior schools, which trust us to instil valuable personal qualities in our girls, such as resilience, independence and adaptability to change. In addition, we proactively support parents by offering all the information they need to make an informed choice when selecting the right school for their daughter.
Do you collaborate with Wetherby School?
Yes. Throughout every academic year, our girls regularly join boys from Wetherby School, which is next door at 11 Pembridge Square, in engaging extracurricular activities. Examples include Year 3 boys’ ‘Maker Market’, to which our Year 3 girls are invited, and reading sessions with our older girls and boys in younger year groups.
Many of our girls have brothers at Wetherby School, meaning shared activities have an added layer of enrichment and enjoyment. In addition, we plan on extending this programme by adding larger shared events very soon.
Which clubs do you offer and do you provide wraparound care?
Our expansive club programme is designed to enrich girls' experience at school by instilling strong personal qualities and promoting development in diverse areas. Extracurricular activities are integral to school life, and our girls enjoy access to over 70 clubs to inspire and motivate them each week. In addition, by fully engaging in these stimulating, educative projects, our students learn to cultivate key life skills, such as teamwork, leadership and confidence. For further details of our extensive offering, we invite you to explore the exciting opportunities under Extracurricular Activities.
Pembridge Hall endeavours to support busy, working parents by offering wraparound care in conjunction with our club programme. For this reason, girls have the option to attend our Early Club from 8:00am and/or after-school sessions until 5:00pm, enjoying games and various activities, and meeting other learners from across the school.
If you still have a question about our school and how your daughter can benefit from an exceptional all-rounded education, fill in the Enquiry Form below and a member of our team will get back to you.
